import numpy as np

def binary_symmetric_channel_capacity(crossover_prob):
    if crossover_prob == 0 or crossover_prob == 1:
        return 1.0
    h_p = -crossover_prob * np.log2(crossover_prob) - (1 - crossover_prob) * np.log2(1 - crossover_prob)
    capacity = 1 - h_p
    return capacity

def channel_capacity_blahut_arimoto(channel_matrix, max_iter=1000, tol=1e-8):
    n_inputs, n_outputs = channel_matrix.shape
    r = np.ones(n_inputs) / n_inputs
    
    for iteration in range(max_iter):
        q = r @ channel_matrix
        q_safe = np.maximum(q, 1e-15)
        p_x_given_y = (r[:, np.newaxis] * channel_matrix) / q_safe[np.newaxis, :]
        log_update = np.log(np.maximum(p_x_given_y, 1e-15))
        r_new = r * np.exp(np.sum(channel_matrix * log_update, axis=1))
        r_new = r_new / np.sum(r_new)
        
        if np.max(np.abs(r_new - r)) < tol:
            break
        r = r_new
    
    q = r @ channel_matrix
    q_safe = np.maximum(q, 1e-15)
    capacity = np.sum(r[:, np.newaxis] * channel_matrix * np.log(np.maximum(channel_matrix, 1e-15) / q_safe[np.newaxis, :]))
    
    return capacity, r

print(f"BSC capacity (p=0.1): {binary_symmetric_channel_capacity(0.1):.4f} bits")
print(f"BSC capacity (p=0.5): {binary_symmetric_channel_capacity(0.5):.4f} bits")

channel = np.array([[0.9, 0.1], [0.1, 0.9]])
cap, opt_r = channel_capacity_blahut_arimoto(channel)
print(f"Channel capacity: {cap:.4f} bits")
